prompt: Which two files contained the regex we identified as exponentially backtracking, and what was the bad pattern?
context: [USER] Our log ingestion service has started pegging a CPU at 100% on a small fraction of log lines. Help me find the ReDoS.
[AGENT] Sure. Tell me the stack.
[USER] Go 1.21, regex from stdlib. We log JSON-structured lines but some legacy services still emit plain-text, so we have a fallback parser.
[AGENT] Go's regexp/syntax uses RE2 and is NOT vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking. Are you sure it's regexp stdlib?
[USER] Hmm good point. Let me check... OK we use dlclark/regexp2 for some patterns because we needed lookbehind. That's .NET-style and CAN backtrack.
[AGENT] That's the likely culprit. Let me grep for regexp2 usage.
[TOOL:grep] 'regexp2\\.' --include='*.go' /srv/log-ingestor
[TOOL_OUTPUT] /srv/log-ingestor/internal/parse/legacy_parser.go: 4 matches. /srv/log-ingestor/internal/parse/timestamp.go: 2 matches. /srv/log-ingestor/internal/filter/priority_filter.go: 1 match.
[AGENT] Let me look at legacy_parser.go first.
[TOOL:read] /srv/log-ingestor/internal/parse/legacy_parser.go
[TOOL_OUTPUT] var legacyLinePattern = regexp2.MustCompile(`^(?<ts>\\S+\\s+\\S+)\\s+(?<sev>[A-Z]+)\\s+(?<msg>(.|\\s)*?)(\\s+at\\s+)?(?<stack>.*)$`, regexp2.Multiline)
[AGENT] Found a suspicious pattern. That `(.|\\s)*?` combined with `(\\s+at\\s+)?` and `.*` at the end can create exponential alternatives. Let me test.
[TOOL:bash] echo 'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA at AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA' | ./test-regex-bench
[TOOL_OUTPUT] Match took 8.2 seconds for 50-char input. Input size 60 chars takes 33 seconds.
[AGENT] Confirmed ReDoS. Let me check timestamp.go too.
[TOOL:read] /srv/log-ingestor/internal/parse/timestamp.go
[TOOL_OUTPUT] var ambiguousTimestamp = regexp2.MustCompile(`^(\\d+[-/]?)+(\\s+(\\d+:?)+)?$`, regexp2.None)

[AGENT] Another one. `(\\d+[-/]?)+` is the classic exponential-overlap pattern. So we have two bad regexes: in legacy_parser.go the pattern `^(?<ts>\\S+\\s+\\S+)\\s+(?<sev>[A-Z]+)\\s+(?<msg>(.|\\s)*?)(\\s+at\\s+)?(?<stack>.*)$` and in timestamp.go the pattern `^(\\d+[-/]?)+(\\s+(\\d+:?)+)?$`. [AGENT] On it...
[... 40 turns of rewrite, benchmark, test, review ...]
